discriminating_observations: If the braking-box endpoint tip speed is materially below the recorded-input endpoint tip speed (beyond numerical noise), the recorded input was not at locally available braking authority at this state and horizon (supports H2).

If the two endpoint tip speeds are nearly equal, the recorded input is already at, or indistinguishable from, the locally available braking authority for a 0.01 s interval under the 8 N limits (supports H1).
If the endpoint speed difference is within numerical noise while endpoint position differences also show no consistent ordering, the probe cannot rank the inputs at 0.01 s (supports H3).
The recorded-vs-braking input norms indicate whether the recorded tensions were anywhere near the recorded per-channel force limits, which is contextual evidence only, not a cause.
hypotheses: H1 (limited recorded braking authority): at the saved projected state of update 33, the recorded applied tensions already deliver endpoint braking close to the maximum obtainable in one 0.01 s interval under the recorded 8 N per-channel tendon limits, so an instantaneous braking-box input yields an endpoint tip speed and position nearly equal to the recorded input.

H2 (recorded plan not braking-limited): at the same saved projected state, an instantaneous braking-box input yields a materially lower predicted endpoint tip speed than the recorded applied input, i.e. the recorded input is not at the locally available braking authority for this state and horizon, consistent with a recorded objective that carries no terminal/holding tip-speed penalty.
H3 (probe insensitive): the two inputs produce endpoint tip speeds that differ only within numerical noise at 0.01 s, so this projected-model probe cannot rank them at all.
local_question: At the single saved projected state of controller update 33 (t = 0.33 s, the retained late-window state at the highest recorded late tip speed), does an instantaneous braking-box input produce a lower predicted endpoint tip speed and world-tip position error over the fixed 0.01 s projected horizon than the recorded applied input, and by how much?
unresolved: This projection-braking comparison cannot establish closed-loop settling behaviour or a dominant cause, and a 0.01 s projected-model probe cannot explain the entire settling failure.

Objective weighting (terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight recorded 0.0, holding_brake_lead_s 0.0, velocity/terminal_velocity weights 1e-4, tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02), plan-selection/warm-start behaviour (initialization_selected 29 vs noninitialization_selected 6, regenerate_warm_states true, feasible_return budget 15 s / relative improvement 0.1), and effective-horizon truncation (2 intervals at update 33, 1 at update 34 vs configured horizon 10) are not separable by this check if they predict the same endpoint difference.

Backend-model mismatch between the projected GVS state and the full serial-backend response is not represented by this short-horizon probe, and the endpoint prediction does not measure full-state agreement.

Wall-clock solver/deadline degradation (mean update 17.0752 s, 35 deadline misses, 34 User_Requested_Stop vs 1 Solve_Succeeded, max_cpu_s 30.0) is a recorded wall-timing property; this probe cannot measure its effect on physical tip motion and retained notes state wall misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time.

Historical optimizer iterations, per-iteration objective contributions and full warm plans are not retained (source.historical_full_plans retained=false; full_snapshots_available false), so no retained signal here can attribute the residual tip speed.
